34.0.0.en: The plains of Moab: the eastern plain of the Jordan valley, immediately north of the Dead Sea.

34.0.1.en: Moses went up to Mount Nebo, which is one of the chain of the mountains of Abarim, and the top of Pisgah is its highest peak (Map 6, 8), which lies on the eastern bank of the Jordan opposite Jericho, which lies to its west. From there the Lord showed him the land that He would give to His people, in its various parts, and the first part mentioned was from Gilead to Dan. Gilead extends from east of the Jordan to the border of the Arabian desert, while Dan is the region that was called Laish and was then invaded by the tribe of Dan, which settled in it, and it is at the farthest north of the country (ch. 33:22, Judg 18).

34.1.0.en: The second part lies west of the Jordan and includes:

34.1.1.en: The lands of Naphtali: opposite the region that Dan seized in the north.

34.1.2.en: The land of Ephraim: it is west of the Jordan, opposite the land of Gad on its east.

34.1.3.en: And Manasseh: the part that lies west of the Jordan, in continuation of the portion of the half-tribe east of the Jordan.

34.1.4.en: All the land of Judah unto the utmost sea: central and southern Palestine, from the Dead Sea to the Mediterranean Sea.

34.2.1.en: The south: southern Palestine, the Negev.

34.2.2.en: The plain: as the inspired text explains it, it includes the area of Jericho, the city of palm trees, that is, the region of Jericho lying west of the Jordan, whose site is now Tell es-Sultan. It was called the city of palm trees because palm trees abound in it. Unto Zoar: on the southeastern shore of the Dead Sea.

34.3.0.en: By Moses' seeing the land that He swore to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the Lord wanted to reassure him about the fate of his people, who would possess those lands, but He would not allow him to cross into it because he did not glorify the Lord with fitting glorification in the incident of striking the rock twice (Num 20:10-12).

34.3.1.en: As Moses looked toward the Promised Land, would that you lifted your eyes toward heaven and contemplated the beauty of the eternity God has prepared for you, so that your spiritual feelings are stirred and you become zealous for life with Him and for drawing souls to prepare with you for the Kingdom.

34.4.s.en: (2) The death of Moses and Joshua taking up the leadership

34.4.1.en: Beth-peor: a temple of the god Peor, the god of the Moabites (Num 23:28) (Map 15). Moses died after he had looked upon the Promised Land and been comforted by God's promises that He gives to His children, and God took his body and buried it in the plain opposite Beth-peor. He hid his body lest the children of Israel find it and worship it because of their great love for him. His body remained hidden until the day this chapter was written, which was written by Moses' disciple Joshua the son of Nun, and his body is still hidden to this day. The devil tried to reveal the body of Moses, but the archangel Michael rebuked him and prevented him by the power of God from revealing the body, lest he lead the children of Israel astray (Jude 9).

34.5.0.en: God gave Moses health until the end of his life, so he was full of vitality though his age had reached one hundred and twenty years, and likewise his eyesight remained strong so that he was able to see the Promised Land from afar.

34.6.0.en: The period of mourning for Moses extended for a month of time, which is the longest period of mourning for great men. The Jews wept for him greatly because of their great love for him and his great standing among them. They had likewise wept for his brother Aaron for a month (Num 20:29), a period which signifies perfection.

34.7.0.en: The Lord had previously asked Moses, near the end of his life, to lay his hand on Joshua to consecrate him for succeeding him in leading the people (Num 27:16-23), for God pours out upon him His holy gifts by the laying on of hands. And as the children of Israel listened to Moses, they listened to Joshua, because the Lord placed awe upon him, just as Moses commanded them to obey him.

34.7.1.en: Here appears the rite of the laying on of hands, which was confirmed in the New Testament (Acts 13:3) in the ordination of bishops and priests, and the Church practices it to this day.

34.8.0.en: The service of Moses, extending forty years, and his works were not enjoyed by another after him, in addition to the patience, longsuffering and forbearance toward the stubborn people with which he was adorned. He alone had a special dealing with the Lord in speaking directly with Him (Num 12:6-8).

34.9.0.en: God worked through Moses great miracles that He did not work with any prophet, which appeared in the ten plagues, the parting of the Red Sea, and God's care for His people in the wilderness for forty years, so that the Church calls him the chief of the prophets.

34.9.1.en: In proportion to your humility and submission to God, His work is manifested in you and He reveals Himself to you so that you enjoy His fellowship, and He defeats your enemies under your feet so that you live reassured and joyful.

34.9.2.en: A comparison between Moses the prophet and Christ. Moses was a type of the Lord of glory Jesus Christ in many respects, the most important of which are:

34.9.3.en: 1- God chose Moses from the midst of his people to be a prophet and leader to them (Deut 18:15), and likewise Christ was chosen by Him from among His people to save them and redeem them (Jn 1:11, Mt 1:3, 16).

34.9.4.en: 2- Moses was subjected in his infancy to a plot to destroy him by a wicked king, Pharaoh, and God rescued him from his hand by a great miracle, and many children died in this plot (Ex 2). Likewise King Herod tried to kill Christ in His infancy, but He fled to Egypt, and Herod killed many children in Bethlehem (Mt 2).

34.9.5.en: 3- Moses lived a period of time in Egypt, the first forty years of his life, and then returned to it to bring his people out of it (Ex 2). And Christ fled to Egypt in His infancy and lived in it for a period of time and blessed it, and then returned to Judea (Mt 2).

34.9.6.en: 4- Moses went down after forty years to visit his people to set them free by his strength, and then returned after another forty years to visit them and set them free by the power of God (Ex 4:29-31). And the Lord Jesus Christ became incarnate to visit His people, and He went about everywhere doing good (Lk 1:68-78).

34.9.7.en: 5- Moses left the glory of the royal palace and went down to visit his people (Ex 3) to share their sufferings. And Christ came down from heaven incarnate to share our humanity (Phil 2:5-8).

34.9.8.en: 6- When Moses tried to break up the quarrel between the two Jewish men, the wrongdoer resisted him. Likewise when Christ came to save His people, the priests and Pharisees rose up against Him and crucified Him.

34.9.9.en: 7- Moses worked miracles to prove to his people and to Pharaoh that he was sent by God. And Christ performed many miracles to prove His divinity and that He is from heaven.

34.9.10.en: 8- God spoke to His people through Moses, for He spoke to him and he told the people God's commands (Ex 19:7, 20:22). And in Christ the Word of God appeared to the whole world, so God spoke to His people through His life on earth (Jn 1:1, 14).

34.9.11.en: 9- Moses fasted forty days to receive the commandments and the Law (Ex 24:18, 34:28), and Christ fasted forty days and was tempted by the devil (Mt 4) before beginning His ministry and giving humanity His life-giving words.

34.9.12.en: 10- God gave His Law to Moses on the mountain (Ex 19, 20). Likewise Christ gave His Law in His Sermon on the Mount (Mt 5, 6, 7).

34.9.13.en: 11- The face of Moses shone after he saw God (Ex 34:29, 30). And Christ's face shone in His Transfiguration on the mountain (Mt 17:1, 2, Mk 9:2-6).

34.9.14.en: 12- The glory of God appeared before Moses in the cloud and the thick darkness on the mountain when he received the Law, and a cloud surrounded Christ on the Mount of Transfiguration, and at His ascension a cloud took Him out of the sight of His disciples.

34.9.15.en: 13- God bore witness to Moses and glorified him before his brothers Aaron and Miriam (Num 12:8), and the Father bore witness to Christ at His baptism and in His Transfiguration by His saying "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 3:17, 17:5) and His saying another time "I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again" (Jn 12:28).

34.9.16.en: 14- Moses was followed by twelve tribes and seventy elders (Num 1, Ex 24:1, Num 11:16), and Christ had twelve disciples and seventy apostles (Mt 10:1, Lk 9:1, 10:1).

34.9.17.en: 15- Moses appeared after his death in the Transfiguration on the mountain with Christ and Elijah (Mt 17:3), and Christ appeared after His death and resurrection to His disciples and to many (Mt 28:9, Mk 16, 1 Cor 15:5-8).

34.9.18.en: 16- Moses declared his readiness to redeem his people by having his name blotted out of the book of life for the sake of the salvation of his people (Ex 32:32). And Christ actually redeemed His people on the Cross.

34.9.19.en: 17- Moses died on a high place, Mount Nebo (Deut 34:1, 5), and Christ died on a high place, the Cross.

34.9.20.en: 18- Moses resembled Christ in many qualities, such as:

34.9.21.en: a – Being mighty in words and deeds (Acts 7:22, Lk 2:47).

34.9.25.en: 19- Moses resembled Christ in many offices, such as:

34.9.29.en: d – Mediation of the covenant (Ex 20:23, Isa 55:3-5).

34.9.30.en: e- Legislation: each of them gave the Law to his people.

34.9.31.en: f - Founding the Church: Moses established the tent of meeting, a type of the Church (Ex 40), and Christ founded the Church (Mt 16:18).

34.9.34.en: 20- The life of Moses was accompanied by many phenomena that signify important matters in the New Testament with Christ, the most important of which are:

34.9.35.en: a – The bush: as a type of the Incarnation of Christ from the Virgin.

34.9.36.en: b - Crossing the Red Sea as a type of Baptism (1 Cor 10:2).

34.9.37.en: c - The manna: a type of the Body and Blood of the Lord (Jn 6:35, 50).

34.9.38.en: d – The rock from which the water comes out as a type of Christ (1 Cor 10).

34.9.39.en: e- The rod of Moses as a type of the Cross.

34.9.40.en: f - Circumcision as a type of Baptism.

34.9.41.en: g - The bronze serpent as a type of Christ (Jn 3:14).

34.9.42.en: h - The sacrifices, a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross.

34.9.43.en: i - The feasts in the Old Testament as a type of the feasts in the New Testament.

34.9.44.en: j - The lifting up of Moses' hands in prayer in his war against Amalek (Ex 17) as a type of the Cross.

34.9.45.en: k - The tent of meeting, a type of the Church of the New Testament.
